    Proposition 7.5: the residual characters are part of an integer basis #

    That paper (prop:primitive-parameter-characters): "In the weight lattice L = W(P), the residual characters χ_i form part of an integer basis."

    Here χ_i = w(p_i) − ν_{v_i} for a mesh weight W_u with values in W(P) restricting to the identity (Lemma 7.4 with h = id). Given integer mesh weights W_j with W_j(p_i) − ν_{v_i} = δ_ij (residual_dual), the integer ray weights h_j = res W_j satisfy h_j(χ_i) = δ_ij: the mesh weights h_j ∘ W_u and W_j have the same restriction, so by Lemma 7.4 they differ by object values vanishing at the projectives, which do not change the weight of a row relative to its mesh (rowWt_eq_of_res). As W(P) is free of finite rank, the χ_i are part of a basis (exists_basis_of_dual).

    Deviation: the source identifies χ_i with the deck class ±θ_{g_i} and uses a lemma on the periodic core; we use the dual mesh weights instead.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
